title: R’ Yaakov, Son of R’ Elazar
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R’ Yaakov son of R’ Elazar.

Midrash Tehillim 19:2 cites him saying, “They knew that their God is truthful, and they do not flatter Him.” A parallel appears in Yoma 69b under R’ Elazar. Hyman reports that the glosses of רש״ב on Tehillim say it SHOULD READ R’ Yaakov bar Elazar. Hyman calls this mistaken: the glossator overlooked Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7:3 and the end of Megillah, chapter 3, where, he says, the correct reading is R’ Yitzchak son of R’ Elazar. Hyman claims that Midrash Tehillim had the initials R-Y, which became R’ Yaakov, and that in Yoma the name R’ Yaakov was lost, leaving only R’ Elazar.

notes.text: The checked Midrash Tehillim 19:2 names Yaakov son of Elazar. Hyman argues instead for Yitzchak, yet his final sentence again says Yaakov was lost from Yoma. That internal discrepancy is preserved. רש״ב is retained as Rashab without assigning a new personal identity.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier MidrashTehillim19:2 match remains inherited, not a new whole-source inspection. Hyman says the רש״ב gloss SHOULD READ Yaakov bar Elazar, condemns that gloss as mistaken, advocates Yitzchak son of Elazar, yet ends with Yaakov allegedly lost in Yoma. This internal discrepancy is retained at full force. Buber is only an unverified lead; no gloss was supplied. The name Elazar in the gloss’s bar Elazar has no inserted father title. All uninspected personal titles remain R-prime, and the initials/name-loss history remains Hyman’s claim.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud texts both name Yitzchak: Berakhot 7:3 has R. Yitzchak ben Elazar and Megillah 3:7 has R. Yitzchak bar La’zar. The consulted Midrash Tehillim 19:2 names Yaakov son of Elazar. Yoma 69b names Elazar and says that the prophets did not speak falsely about God. Hyman’s printed article (vol. II, pp. 777–778) itself ends by saying that Yaakov was lost from Yoma. His account of the initials and the loss of the name remains conjectural. The cited gloss has not been independently collated.
